claim: RNF43 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase and known negative regulator of WNT/β-catenin signaling.
source: RNF43 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase and known negative regulator of WNT/β-catenin signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: RNF43 is a regulator of noncanonical WNT5A-induced signaling in human cells.
source: We demonstrate that RNF43 is also a regulator of noncanonical WNT5A-induced signaling in human cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through multiple experiments in the results section.

claim: RNF43 can interact with ROR1, ROR2, VANGL1, and VANGL2.
source: Analysis of the RNF43 interactome using BioID and immunoprecipitation showed that RNF43 can interact with the core receptor complex components dedicated to the noncanonical Wnt pathway such as ROR1, ROR2, VANGL1, and VANGL2.
evidence: This is supported by BioID mass spectrometry data (Figure 1D) and co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 2).

claim: RNF43 triggers VANGL2 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.
source: RNF43 triggers VANGL2 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and clathrin-dependent internalization of ROR1 receptor and inhibits ROR2 activation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by His-ubiquitin pulldown assays (Figure 3A) and proteasome inhibitor experiments (Figure 3C).

claim: RNF43 triggers clathrin-dependent internalization of ROR1 receptor.
source: RNF43 triggers VANGL2 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and clathrin-dependent internalization of ROR1 receptor and inhibits ROR2 activation.
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry (Figure 3E-F) and dansylcadaverine inhibition experiments (Figure 3F).

claim: RNF43 inhibits ROR2 activation.
source: RNF43 triggers VANGL2 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and clathrin-dependent internalization of ROR1 receptor and inhibits ROR2 activation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis showing changes in ROR2 protein levels (Figure 6B).

claim: RNF43 blocks pro-metastatic WNT5A signaling in melanoma.
source: These activities of RNF43 are physiologically relevant and block pro-metastatic WNT5A signaling in melanoma.
evidence: This is supported by functional assays including wound healing, invasion, and invadopodia formation assays (Figure 5).

claim: RNF43 inhibits responses to WNT5A, which results in the suppression of invasive properties of melanoma cells.
source: RNF43 inhibits responses to WNT5A, which results in the suppression of invasive properties of melanoma cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by multiple functional assays in melanoma cell lines (Figure 5).

claim: RNF43 prevented WNT5A-assisted development of resistance to BRAF V600E and MEK inhibitors.
source: Furthermore, RNF43 prevented WNT5A-assisted development of resistance to BRAF V600E and MEK inhibitors.
evidence: This is shown by resistance acquisition experiments (Figure 6G, 6L).

claim: RNF43 acted as melanoma suppressor and improved response to targeted therapies in vivo.
source: Next, RNF43 acted as melanoma suppressor and improved response to targeted therapies in vivo.
evidence: This is demonstrated by mouse xenograft experiments (Figure 7).

claim: RNF43 expression decreases during melanoma progression.
source: In line with these findings, RNF43 expression decreases during melanoma progression and RNF43-low patients have a worse prognosis.
evidence: This is shown by analysis of gene expression datasets (Figure 4A, 4B).

claim: RNF43-low patients have a worse prognosis.
source: In line with these findings, RNF43 expression decreases during melanoma progression and RNF43-low patients have a worse prognosis.
evidence: This is demonstrated by survival analysis (Figure 4C).

claim: RNF43 is a newly discovered negative regulator of WNT5A-mediated biological responses that desensitizes cells to WNT5A.
source: We conclude that RNF43 is a newly discovered negative regulator of WNT5A-mediated biological responses that desensitizes cells to WNT5A.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all experimental data.

claim: Removal of endogenous WNT5A in T-REx 293 cells is sufficient to eliminate the activation of readouts of WNT5A signaling such as phosphorylation of ROR1, DVL2, and DVL3.
source: Removal of endogenous WNT5A in T-REx 293 cells is sufficient to eliminate the activation of readouts of WNT5A signaling such as phosphorylation of ROR1, DVL2, and DVL3 that can be monitored by western blotting as the decrease in the phosphorylation-mediated electrophoretic mobility shifts (Figure 1A; Bryja et al., 2007b; Kotrbová et al., 2020; Radaszkiewicz and Bryja, 2020).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis comparing wild-type and WNT5A KO cells (Figure 1A).

claim: Autocrine WNT5A signaling was promoted by the inhibition of endogenous RNF43/ZNRF3 by RSPO1 treatment.
source: Autocrine WNT5A signaling was promoted by the inhibition of endogenous RNF43/ZNRF3 by RSPO1 treatment (Figure 1B, compare lanes 1 and 2)
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis (Figure 1B).

claim: Autocrine WNT5A signaling was inhibited by RNF43 overexpression under the tetracycline (Tet)-controlled promoter (TetON) or by block of WNT secretion using Porcupine inhibitor Wnt-C59.
source: Autocrine WNT5A signaling was promoted by the inhibition of endogenous RNF43/ZNRF3 by RSPO1 treatment (Figure 1B, compare lanes 1 and 2) and inhibited by RNF43 overexpression under the tetracycline (Tet)-controlled promoter (TetON) or by block of WNT secretion using Porcupine inhibitor Wnt-C59 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis (Figure 1B).

claim: Overexpression of RNF43 completely blocked signaling induced by recombinant WNT5A.
source: As shown in Figure 1C, overexpression of RNF43 completely blocked signaling induced by recombinant WNT5A.
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis of cells treated with increasing doses of rhWNT5A (Figure 1C).

claim: Several core proteins of the noncanonical Wnt signaling pathway – namely, ROR1, ROR2, VANGL1, VANGL2, SEC24B, and all three isoforms of DVL – were strongly and specifically biotinylated by RNF43-BirA*.
source: Several core proteins of the noncanonical Wnt signaling pathway – namely, ROR1, ROR2, VANGL1, VANGL2, SEC24B, and all three isoforms of DVL – were strongly and specifically biotinylated by RNF43-BirA* (Figure 1D and D′, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by BioID mass spectrometry analysis (Figure 1D).

claim: RNF43 co-immunoprecipitated with both VANGL2 and VANGL1.
source: RNF43 co-immunoprecipitated with both VANGL2 (Figure 2A) and VANGL1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).

claim: VANGL2 and RNF43 co-localize in the cell membrane.
source: More detailed analysis of VANGL2 showed co-localization of VANGL2 and RNF43 in the cell membrane (Figure 2B and B′).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence microscopy (Figure 2B).

claim: RNF43 efficiently pulled down ROR1 and ROR2.
source: RNF43 also efficiently pulled down ROR1 (Figure 2C) and ROR2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Deletion of the cysteine-rich domain (CRD) of ROR2 had no impact on the amount of co-immunoprecipitated RNF43, which suggests that RNF43 primarily interacts with RORs intracellularly.
source: Deletion of the cysteine-rich domain (CRD) (ROR2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) had no impact on the amount of co-immunoprecipitated RNF43, which suggests that RNF43 primarily interacts with RORs intracellularly.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation with ROR2 deletion mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Both ROR1/ROR2 co-localized with RNF43 at the level of the plasma membrane.
source: Both ROR1/ROR2 co-localized with RNF43 at the level of the plasma membrane (Figure 2D and D′ and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and C′).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence microscopy (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).

claim: RNF43 was able to bind both VANGL2 and ROR1 as efficiently in DVL triple knockout cells as in wild-type cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E, RNF43 was able to bind both VANGL2 and ROR1 as efficiently as in the wild-type cells (compare with Figure 2A and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in DVL triple knockout cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).

claim: RNF43 interacts with PCP proteins from VANGL and ROR families in a DVL-independent way.
source: In summary, our results indicate that RNF43 interacts, in a DVL-independent way, with PCP proteins from VANGL and ROR families.
evidence: This is concluded from co-immunoprecipitation experiments in DVL triple knockout cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).

claim: VANGL2 was ubiquitinated when co-expressed with RNF43 but not with RNF43 Mut1.
source: Using His-ubiquitin pulldown assay, we were able to show that VANGL2 (Figure 3A), as well as DVL1 and DVL2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), was ubiquitinated when co-expressed with RNF43 but not with RNF43 Mut1.
evidence: This is demonstrated by His-ubiquitin pulldown assay (Figure 3A).

claim: DVL1 and DVL2 were ubiquitinated when co-expressed with RNF43 but not with RNF43 Mut1.
source: Using His-ubiquitin pulldown assay, we were able to show that VANGL2 (Figure 3A), as well as DVL1 and DVL2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), was ubiquitinated when co-expressed with RNF43 but not with RNF43 Mut1.
evidence: This is demonstrated by His-ubiquitin pulldown assay (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).

claim: RNF43-induced ubiquitination of ROR1 or ROR2 was not detected.
source: However, we were unable to detect RNF43-induced ubiquitination of ROR1 or ROR2 (negative data, not shown).
evidence: This is stated as a negative result in the text.

claim: Overexpression of RNF43, but not its E3 ligase dead variant, decreased VANGL2 protein level.
source: Further analysis showed that overexpression of RNF43, but not its E3 ligase dead variant, decreased VANGL2 protein level (Figure 3B, quantified in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis (Figure 3B).

claim: Decrease in VANGL2 caused by RNF43 was accompanied by impeded phosphorylation of ROR1 and DVL3.
source: Decrease in VANGL2 caused by RNF43 was accompanied by impeded phosphorylation of ROR1 (Figure 3B) and DVL3 (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis (Figure 3B).

claim: Two independent clones of cells deficient in both RNF43 and ZNRF3 showed higher VANGL2 levels and higher DVL phosphorylation.
source: On the other side, two independent clones of cells deficient in both RNF43 and ZNRF3 (RNF43/ZNRF3 dKO; R/Z dKO) showed higher VANGL2 levels and higher DVL phosphorylation (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis (Figure 3B).

claim: Treatment with the proteasome inhibitor MG132 but not with autophagosome-lysosome inhibitor chloroquine blocked the effects of RNF43 on VANGL2 and DVL phosphorylation.
source: Interestingly, treatment with the proteasome inhibitor MG132 but not with autophagosome-lysosome inhibitor chloroquine blocked these effects of RNF43 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis with proteasome and lysosome inhibitors (Figure 3C).

claim: RNF43 action in the noncanonical Wnt pathway depends on the proteasomal degradation pathway.
source: This suggests that RNF43 action in the noncanonical Wnt pathway depends on the proteasomal degradation pathway, which differs from the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, where RNF43 triggers FZD degradation via the lysosomal pathway (Koo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of proteasome vs. lysosome inhibitors (Figure 3C) and comparison with published data.

claim: RNF43 overexpression led to the retention of VANGL2 in the Golgin-97-positive area.
source: However, RNF43 overexpression led to the retention of VANGL2 in the Golgin-97-positive area (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence microscopy (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).

claim: Cells lacking endogenous RNF43 and ZNRF3 have more ROR1 receptor on the surface than parental T-REx cells.
source: T-REx cells express dominantly ROR1, and indeed flow cytometric analysis demonstrated that cell lacking endogenous RNF43 and ZNRF3 have more ROR1 receptor on the surface than parental T-REx cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry (Figure 3D).

claim: After 3 hr of tetracycline treatment, decreased surface ROR1 was detected in RNF43/ZNRF3 dKO cells with inducible RNF43.
source: When we introduced inducible RNF43 into RNF43/ZNRF3 dKO T-REx cell line, we were able to rescue this phenotype, and after 3 hr of tetracycline treatment, we detected decreased surface ROR1 and the overnight exposition to tetracycline had no significant effect (Figure 3E and E′).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry (Figure 3E).

claim: Treatment with dansylcadaverine prevented RNF43-mediated effect on the ROR1 surface expression.
source: In agreement with our hypothesis, treatment with this inhibitor prevented RNF43-mediated effect on the ROR1 surface expression in T-REx 293 RNF43/ZNRF3 dKO RNF43 TetON cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry with dansylcadaverine treatment (Figure 3F).

claim: ROR1/RAB5 co-localization was observed after 3 hr of tetracycline treatment and decreased after overnight exposition to tetracycline.
source: Hyperactivation of Rab5 by overexpression of wild-type Rab5 leads to the formation of giant early endosomes (Bucci et al., 1992) where we observed ROR1/RAB5 co-localization after 3 hr of tetracycline treatment. The co-localization decreased after overnight exposition to tetracycline.
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence microscopy (Figure 3G).

claim: RAB11+ endosomes were recruited to the ROR1 after RNF43 induction and RAB11 co-localized strongly with ROR1 even after overnight treatment.
source: RAB11+ endosomes were recruited to the ROR1 as well as after RNF43 induction and RAB11 co-localized strongly with ROR1 even after ON treatment.
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence microscopy (Figure 3G).

claim: Surface ROR1 is controlled by RNF43 via interference with RAB5- and RAB11-mediated endocytosis.
source: We conclude that surface ROR1 is controlled by RNF43 via interference with RAB5- and RAB11-mediated endocytosis and RNF43-mediated effect is not persistent due to the activity of recycling RAB11 recycling pathway (Ullrich et al., 1996).
evidence: This is concluded from immunofluorescence data showing ROR1 co-localization with RAB5 and RAB11 (Figure 3G).

claim: High expression of WNT5A in melanoma is a negative overall survival and positive metastasis formation factor.
source: High expression of WNT5A in this cancer is a negative overall survival and positive metastasis formation factor (Da Forno et al., 2008; Luo et al., 2020; Weeraratna et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Signaling cascade activated by WNT5A in melanoma drives epithelial–mesenchymal transition-like program (EMT), resulting in increased metastatic properties of melanoma cells in vitro and in vivo.
source: Signaling cascade activated by WNT5A in melanoma drives epithelial–mesenchymal transition-like program (EMT), resulting in increased metastatic properties of melanoma cells in vitro and in vivo (Dissanayake et al., 2008; Dissanayake et al., 2007; Sadeghi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: In melanoma, WNT5A acts through FZD and ROR1/ROR2.
source: In melanoma, WNT5A acts through FZD and ROR1/ROR2 (O'Connell et al., 2010; Tiwary and Xu, 2016; Weeraratna et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: RNF43 expression dramatically decreases between benign melanocytic skin nevus and cutaneous melanoma.
source: Interestingly, the in silico analysis of gene expression (Talantov et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2008) showed that RNF43 expression dramatically decreases between benign melanocytic skin nevus and cutaneous melanoma (Figure 4A; Talantov et al., 2005)
evidence: This is shown by analysis of published gene expression datasets (Figure 4A).

claim: RNF43 expression decreases between primary melanoma site and metastasis.
source: RNF43 expression dramatically decreases between benign melanocytic skin nevus and cutaneous melanoma (Figure 4A; Talantov et al., 2005) and further between primary site and metastasis (Xu et al., 2008; Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by analysis of published gene expression datasets (Figure 4B).

claim: RNF43 low melanoma patients have shorter overall survival.
source: Importantly, analysis of other datasets (Anaya, 2016) showed that RNF43 low melanoma patients have shorter overall survival (OS; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by survival analysis (Figure 4C).

claim: ZNRF3 expression had no prognostic value in melanoma.
source: ZNRF3 expression had no prognostic value (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown by survival analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).

claim: The expression of DVL3 and VANGL1 increased during melanoma progression.
source: Interestingly, the expression of two genes encoding direct targets ubiquitinated by RNF43, namely, DVL3 and VANGL1, increased during melanoma progression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C)
evidence: This is shown by gene expression analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).

claim: High expression of DVL3 and VANGL1 correlates with bad prognosis and shorter overall survival in melanoma.
source: the expression of two genes encoding direct targets ubiquitinated by RNF43, namely, DVL3 and VANGL1, increased during melanoma progression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C) and high expression in both cases correlates with bad prognosis and shorter overall survival (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by survival analysis (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).

claim: A375 IV cells secrete higher WNT5A protein levels than parental A375 cell line.
source: WNT5A protein levels are higher and WNT11 levels lower in case of A375 IV metastatic derivate in comparison to parental A375 cell line (Figure 4E′ and E′′).
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis of conditioned media (Figure 4E′).

claim: RNF43 expression in the A375 IV cells was significantly lower than that in the A375 parental cells.
source: Interestingly, RNF43 expression in the A375 IV cells was significantly lower than that in the A375 parental cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).

claim: RNF43 loss- and gain of function correlated strongly with the level of Wnt pathway activation assessed as DVL phosphorylation in A375 derivatives.
source: The initial characterization of A375 derivatives essentially confirmed the findings from T-REx 293 (see Figure 1), where RNF43 loss- and gain of function correlated strongly with the level of Wnt pathway activation assessed as DVL phosphorylation (Figure 4G, quantified in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis (Figure 4G).

claim: In A375, A375 IV, and A2058 melanoma cells RNF43 overexpression efficiently blocked WNT5A-induced signaling.
source: Similarly to T-REx 293 cells, in A375 (Figure 4H), A375 IV (Figure 4I), and A2058 (Figure 4J and quantified effect of RNF43 OE on the endogenous WNT pathway activity in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G and H) melanoma cells RNF43 overexpression efficiently blocked WNT5A-induced signaling.
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis (Figure 4H, 4I, 4J).

claim: All A375, A375 IV, and A2078 cells overexpressing RNF43 showed suppressed 2D collective migration in the wound healing assay.
source: Firstly, all A375, A375 IV, and A2078 cells overexpressing RNF43 showed suppressed 2D collective migration in the wound healing assay (Figure 5A–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by wound healing assays (Figure 5A-E).

claim: A375 IV and A2058 cell lines showed significant response to CCL21 and CXCL12 in collagen I hydrogel invasion assay and RNF43 blocked completely these invasion events.
source: A375 IV and A2058 cell lines showed significant response to these treatments and RNF43 blocked completely these invasion events (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by collagen I hydrogel 3D invasion assay (Figure 5G and H).

claim: The response of A375 cells in collagen I hydrogel invasion assay was negligible, confirming their decreased metastatic capacity compared to the A375 IV.
source: Importantly, the response of A375 cells in this assay was negligible (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), confirming their decreased metastatic capacity compared to the A375 IV.
evidence: This is shown by collagen I hydrogel invasion assay (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Invasion of individual cells through Matrigel was higher in A375 IV in comparison to A375 but in both cases reduced by RNF43 OE.
source: In line, invasion of individual cells through the extracellular matrix (ECM) mimicking Matrigel was higher in A375 IV in comparison to A375 but in both cases reduced by RNF43 OE (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by Matrigel invasion assay (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).

claim: A375 IV cells formed more invadopodia than A375 parental cells and cells overexpressing RNF43 formed less of them.
source: A375 IV cells formed more invadopodia than A375 parental cells (Figure 5I) and cells overexpressing RNF43 formed less of them (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by invadopodia formation assay (Figure 5I).

claim: Reduced gelatin degradation activity was observed in A375 and A375 IV cells overexpressing RNF43.
source: In agreement, we also observed reduced gelatin degradation activity in A375 and A375 IV cells overexpressing RNF43 (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gelatin degradation assay (Figure 5J).

claim: Treatment with WNT5A enhanced the gelatin degradation capacity of A375 cells, but not their RNF43-overexpressing derivate.
source: Furthermore, treatment with WNT5A enhanced the gelatin degradation capacity of A375 cells, but not their RNF43-overexpressing derivate (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is demonstrated by gelatin degradation assay with WNT5A treatment (Figure 5J).

claim: Transient exposition to vemurafenib resulted in the impeded phosphorylation of ROR1, DVL2, and DVL3 and increased ROR2 protein level without change in its mRNA.
source: Interestingly, transient exposition to vemurafenib resulted in the impeded phosphorylation of ROR1, DVL2, and DVL3 and increased ROR2 protein level without change in its mRNA (Figure 6B–D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is shown by western blot and RT-qPCR analysis (Figure 6B-D).

claim: Vemurafenib-resistant cells displayed elevated ROR1 levels (both protein and mRNA) and increased phosphorylation of DVL2 and DVL3.
source: On the other side, VR cells displayed elevated ROR1 levels (both protein and mRNA) and increased phosphorylation of DVL2 and DVL3 (Figure 6B–D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot and RT-qPCR analysis (Figure 6B-D).

claim: The expression of WNT5A was higher in the resistant VR cells.
source: Strikingly, the expression of WNT5A was also higher in the resistant VR cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR analysis (Figure 6E).

claim: Exogenous RNF43 decreased colony formation and proliferation of cells seeded in low density and vemurafenib further enhanced this effect.
source: As shown in Figure 6F, exogenous RNF43 decreased colony formation and proliferation of cells seeded in low density and vemurafenib further enhanced this effect.
evidence: This is demonstrated by colony formation assay (Figure 6F).

claim: Both A375 and A375 IV-overexpressing RNF43 completely failed to develop resistance to vemurafenib and died off during selection at 1 μM vemurafenib concentration.
source: Importantly, both A375 and A375 IV-overexpressing RNF43 completely failed to develop resistance to vemurafenib and died off during selection at 1 μM vemurafenib concentration (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is shown by long-term vemurafenib resistance acquisition experiments (Figure 6G).

claim: A2058 enriched with ectopically expressed RNF43 did not survive cobimetinib monotherapy and cobimetinib with vemurafenib combination.
source: A2058 enriched with ectopically expressed RNF43 did not survive cobimetinib monotherapy and cobimetinib with vemurafenib combination, whereas vemurafenib-only treatment did not fully eliminate those cells (Figure 6L).
evidence: This is demonstrated by resistance acquisition experiments (Figure 6L).

claim: VANGL1 showed a shift in all delivered resistance models, while VANGL2 was shifted only in cells being in the long-term culture with cobimetinib and with cobimetinib and vemurafenib.
source: Firstly, we noticed the shift of VANGL1 in all delivered resistance models, while VANGL2 was shifted only in cells being in the long-term culture with cobimetinib and with cobimetinib and vemurafenib (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis (Figure 6H).

claim: Both MITF protein level and MITF gene expression increased in VR cells and decreased in all cobimetinib-insensitive lines.
source: Interestingly, both MITF protein level and MITF gene expression increased in VR cells and decreased in all cobimetinib-insensitive lines (Figure 6H and I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot and RT-qPCR analysis (Figure 6H and I).

claim: MITF upregulation was accompanied by clear pigmentation of resistant cells.
source: Moreover, MITF upregulation was accompanied by clear pigmentation of resistant cells (Figure 6I′), suggesting cell phenotype change (Arozarena and Wellbrock, 2019; Ji et al., 2015; Müller et al., 2014).
evidence: This is shown by visual observation of cell pellets (Figure 6I′).

claim: Cohort I (RNF43 low) had significantly shorter survival and formed macroscopic tumors earlier than RNF43 mid and high cohorts.
source: Cohort I (RNF43 low) had significantly shorter survival and formed macroscopic tumors earlier than RNF43 mid and high cohorts (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vivo mouse experiments (Figure 7C).

claim: Tumors originating from cells with the lowest RNF43 expression were significantly bigger than RNF43 mid ones.
source: Moreover, tumors originating from cells with the lowest RNF43 expression were significantly bigger than RNF43 mid ones (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is shown by tumor size measurements (Figure 7D).

claim: The level of RNF43-specific signal in cohorts I–III was significantly and inversely correlated with ROR1 and VANGL2 protein levels and similar trend was also noticed for DVL2 phosphorylation.
source: We found out that the level of RNF43-specific signal in cohorts I–III was significantly and inversely correlated with ROR1 and VANGL2 protein levels and similar trend was also noticed for DVL2 phosphorylation (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E)
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis of tumor lysates and correlation analysis (Figure 7E).

claim: Vemurafenib treatment significantly prolonged the survival in RNF43 mid and RNF43 high cohorts.
source: RNF43 mid and RNF43 high cohorts received vemurafenib, and this treatment significantly prolonged the survival (Figure 7F)
evidence: This is shown by survival analysis (Figure 7F).

claim: Doxycycline supplementation (RNF43 high) in addition to vemurafenib resulted in the more efficient suppression of tumor growth, suggesting the delayed the BRAFi resistance acquisition.
source: Importantly, doxycycline supplementation (RNF43 high) in addition to vemurafenib resulted in the more efficient suppression of tumor growth, suggesting the delayed the BRAFi resistance acquisition (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by tumor growth measurements (Figure 7G).

claim: The protein level of WNT5A was significantly increased in tumors treated with vemurafenib.
source: Moreover, the protein level of WNT5A was significantly increased in tumors treated with vemurafenib, which could help to bypass the RNF43-related effect as well (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E′′′).
evidence: This is shown by western blot analysis of tumor lysates (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E′′′).
